newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB debenture yield rises to 3.25 pct -- traders.
newsitem.headline: NCB debenture yield rises to 3.25 pct -- traders.

text.p: The yield on Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB)'s new five-year bank debenture with a 2.15 percent coupon rose to 3.25 percent in the secondary market on Tuesday, up from a sell quote of 3.0 percent on Monday, bond traders said.
Approximately 100 million yen worth of the NCB's debenture was traded, they said.
Traders said the recent surge in the NCB's debenture yield and its share price decline were related to the bank's weak capital base and its large exposure to bad loans.
NCB shares closed down 9 yen at 250 on Tuesday. They had fallen to a life-time low of 221 on Monday.
Meanwhile, five-year debentures with a 1.6 percent coupon issued by the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd were quoted at around 1.72 percent.

The Trust Fund of Bureau of Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) holds some 10 trillion yen worth of bank debentures issued by the three long-term credit banks, IBJ, NCB and Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd.
The Trust Fund Bureau does not comment on the breakdown or future investment plans for its debenture holding.
